title: Add LibreWolf as supported browser

workflow: Opus full review, Sol boundary hunter, Opus self-check of the draft, editorial check, batch gates

leads.summary: The new /etc/librewolf/policies.json is not a LibreWolf enterprise-policy input
leads.consequence: After a successful package installation the installer silently writes Omarchy's five Firefox Preferences to /etc/librewolf/policies.json, but Firefox 156's Linux loader looks for /etc/librewolf/policies/policies.json, then falls back to /usr/lib/librewolf/distribution/policies.json. With no existing actual system policy, LibreWolf continues applying its packaged privacy policies and none of Omarchy's new preferences. If the correct system path is populated later, it takes precedence over, not merges with, the package policy. A straightforward path-only correction would consequently suppress LibreWolf's packaged privacy/extension/search policies. Avoid replacing the package file; combine required entries with the distribution policy while preserving package upgrades, or use a supported preference mechanism. The current wrong-path file is unowned by Arch and cannot be picked up via normal package upgrades.
leads.triage: already in Opus final (N1); independent corroboration

leads.summary: The installation and migration apply a distribution-directory purge to the whole /etc/librewolf configuration root
leads.consequence: If /etc/librewolf contains an existing non-root-owned policies/ directory (which is where the application actually reads an administrator's system policy), the install's find -mindepth 1 -maxdepth 1 ! -user root -exec rm -rf deletes the entire tree; a root-owned existing /etc/librewolf/policies.json is unconditionally replaced by the installation, and a directory symlink is unlinked. On an existing installation with this migration still pending, merely having /etc/librewolf makes the migration process it even without LibreWolf being installed: it may delete non-root children and create the unused /etc/librewolf/policies.json. Existing root-owned children other than the directly overwritten policy are preserved; this is conditional on ownership and migration state, not unconditional deletion.
leads.triage: overlaps Opus N3 (user-owned or symlinked /etc/librewolf entries); conditional on unusual setups, not reproduced; kept private

leads.summary: Adding LibreWolf to an old migration does not run it on machines where that migration has already been marked complete
leads.consequence: omarchy-migrate keys execution by filename, not by source content: after the existing 1787515927.sh marker is written, editing BROWSER_POLICY_FIREFOX_DIRS does not cause that migration to run again. Thus machines that already ran it and already have a manually installed LibreWolf and an /etc/librewolf tree get no new policy setup or repair from this change. Selecting LibreWolf as the default also skips the installer when its executable already exists (bin/omarchy-default-browser:43-49). A new migration could cover existing installs, but it must use the real policy path and avoid deleting administrator configuration; running the old migration afresh as written would itself be unsafe for non-root children (CONFIG_PURGE).
leads.triage: consistent with Opus N2 (migration runs once per machine); used in the optional note's 'has not run it yet' qualifier

leads.summary: U+E90F overlaps two divergent open glyph PRs
leads.consequence: Open #12137 uses U+E90F for Brave, #12251 uses U+E90F for Phantombot, while this PR uses it for LibreWolf. When either is merged and the font asset is regenerated, one menu's glyph will display the other's mark unless LibreWolf is reassigned and all menu references updated. The binary fonts and adjacent README lines conflict. The existing charset assertion checks a range, not uniqueness.
leads.triage: already in Opus final; Opus found five claimants, Sol two; coordinator verified five with gh pr diff

leads.summary: Reconcile other divergent browser-policy/browser-registration PRs on merge
leads.consequence: #12148 and #7444 both correct Zen's currently wrong /opt/zen-browser/distribution path, but edit the same BROWSER_POLICY_FIREFOX_DIRS list as this PR. A merge-file using #12148's own base gives conflict markers at exactly that list; resolving by keeping only this PR's side perpetuates Zen's inactive policy. #12132 adds Helium to exact browser argument/menu fixtures, which conflicts with the LibreWolf-only expected list and can fail menu-test when either feature is dropped. #9430 and #12754 similarly add Vivaldi, #8913 edits the Firefox/Zen docs and installer. Preserve all distinct names in header, case, menu and expected lists when these branches merge; neither PR is stacked on #13309. Do not attribute the Zen defect to the LibreWolf PR; it predates this change.
leads.triage: already in Opus final (text conflicts); corroborated

leads.summary: The Firefox-family extension exclusion still omits LibreWolf
leads.consequence: After this PR adds LibreWolf to the supported browsers, the Claude extension explanation says only Firefox and Zen lack support. A LibreWolf user may expect Omarchy to install that Chromium-family extension. Append LibreWolf to the exclusion, while leaving the Chromium-family installation list unchanged.

leads.summary: The newly extended browser introduction says LibreWolf receives a theme it does not receive
leads.consequence: Line 5 now lists LibreWolf among browsers for which installation applies the current Omarchy theme, although the LibreWolf install branch only writes the policy and Wayland flag, and the browser theme setter covers Chromium, Chrome, Edge and Brave. Line 35 explicitly says Firefox, LibreWolf and Zen are not themed. Line 33 also claims Omarchy's default policy is applied to LibreWolf, which is false because of POLICY_PATH. Qualify line 5 for Chromium-family browsers and fix line 33 after correcting the policy target.
leads.triage: factual, verified by coordinator: manual/23-browsers.md:5 'applies your current theme' is contradicted by line 35 and omarchy-theme-set-browser; but the sentence already made that claim for Firefox and Zen at the merge base, the PR only adds LibreWolf to the list. Pre-existing; dropped from public comment

leads.summary: Removing LibreWolf leaves the newly created unowned policy file
leads.consequence: The installer writes /etc/librewolf/policies.json while Arch's librewolf package owns no files under /etc/librewolf; the remover only invokes pacman -Rns and never removes the new file. A remove/reinstall preserves or recreates this orphan. If the policy path is corrected in a later release, add targeted cleanup of this now-unread wrong-path artifact, without removing the user's actual /etc/librewolf/policies/ tree.
leads.triage: already in Opus final (N4, cosmetic, same as Firefox/Zen); dropped

leads.summary: The LibreWolf installer test asserts the unreadable path and stubs every privileged filesystem operation
leads.consequence: A plausible broken installer that writes /etc/librewolf/policies.json, precisely the current implementation, passes all new assertions because sudo only logs invocations and no assertion checks LibreWolf's source-defined policy search or the written file. Add a contract test for /etc/librewolf/policies/policies.json plus a safe isolated file-based fixture or static loader-path assertion, and ensure required upstream policies remain active.
leads.triage: already in Opus final; published as optional note

leads.summary: The migration fixture never asserts LibreWolf's array entry
leads.consequence: A plausible edit removing /etc/librewolf from BROWSER_POLICY_FIREFOX_DIRS leaves the current migration test's 'covers Firefox and Zen' assertion green; existing LibreWolf setups would then receive no hardening from that migration. Add an assertion for the expected LibreWolf directory and a migration fixture for root-owned and non-root children at the real configuration path, without purging arbitrary config.
leads.triage: minor test-only gap without demonstrated benefit; dropped

prior_findings.claim: manual/23-browsers.md:33 'installs a policies file for sensible defaults' untrue for LibreWolf.

/etc/librewolf/policies.json is not read by LibreWolf; loader reads /etc/librewolf/policies/policies.json else distribution/policies.json, never both. Omarchy's five prefs never apply. Moving to policies/ alone would hide LibreWolf's 22 policies permanently.
